subject.title: Stuck-session liveness monitor misclassifies healthy processing runs as stale during event-loop stalls

question: Should OpenClaw change the processing/no-activeWorkKind recovery policy now, or require live measurement proving that healthy active runs can lose diagnostic activity markers during event-loop stalls?
rationale: Current source shows the reported fallthrough, but current tests and recent fixes intentionally preserve aggressive stale-lane recovery, and the issue labels the false-abort chain as likely rather than confirmed.

options.title: Require proof first
options.body: Keep this issue open for a controlled gateway log, Crabbox/live run, or deterministic harness showing a healthy active run reaching stale_session_state and abort_embedded_run.

options.title: Approve a narrow policy change
options.body: Treat processing/no-activeWorkKind as observe-only or long-running and update the existing recovery tests to preserve genuine stale-processing recovery another way.

options.title: Fold into liveness recovery work
options.body: Track this as part of the adjacent stuck-session and event-loop liveness cluster rather than changing the classifier edge independently.

recommendation.title: Require proof first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for a controlled gateway log, Crabbox/live run, or deterministic harness showing a healthy active run reaching stale_session_state and abort_embedded_run.

likelyOwner.reason: They made the latest adjacent recovery-policy change and are well placed to decide whether the current ownerless-lane recovery behavior should be narrowed before live proof exists.
